title: 2021-03-01 Onboarding Retro with Ordna
content:
Date: 1st of March 2021

Attendees: from Ordna team & from the DevOps team.

Ordna resources:

Github: https://github.com/inter-ikea/cbf-re-ipex-ordna-planner

What was discussed

Github migration

The overall consensus was that the migration to Github was quite simple to perform. They set up a Miro todo list to delegate the work among the team. The team will setup a meeting with to show the Miro and allow the DevOps team to improve the documentation available for the work.

The team did encounter some initial issues when migrating from Bitbucket. For example when a review was in progress the linting would not work as expected. This was due to unfamiliarity with the platform and certain features not working as initially expected. There was also an issue with one developer not having access due to not having an IKEA account.

AP DevOps team: Since we have option to onboard users temporarily with work mail to no block activities this should be emphasized during onboarding.

The work was slowed down a bit due to choosing to migrate the codebase as well as change from Jenkins to Github Actions at the same time. The team feel that it was a good choice to do it at the same time and that it helped them improve their pipeline.

Github Actions

Based on an initial spike performed late 2020 the team elected to go with Github Actions for their pipelines. They did feel that had IPEX provided a bit more of guidance and structure the choice could’ve been Azure Pipelines instead. Today they are happy with Github Actions.

Migrating from Jenkins allowed the team to get a better overview of their pipeline and improve it to be more efficient. The UI and UX in Github actions is also an appreciated improvement over Jenkins.

Github Actions workflows

Moving to using YAML to define their workflows took some getting used to but was deemed worth it. It now allows the team to easily configure their build and release flows. They do feel that it would be even better if there was a way to locally test and verify the pipelines without having to commit them to the repository. This is something worth looking into.

Github Advanced Security

The team has chosen to turn of Dependabot alerts as well as security scanning alerts currently. They feel that the amount of PRs opened results in clutter, especially since the team currently doesn’t have time and resources to handle them. The PRs also occupy a ton of build minutes due to running whenever the main branch is updated.

The team will be turning on CodeQL scanning and investigate if they feel that it provides them with any value. They will report back to the DevOps team with their findings.

AP DevOps team: Continue work on IPEX security baseline that will include guidance on how to work with among other things GitHub Advanced Security. See current guideline.

Terraform

The team had an onboarding workshop with on the 23rd of February 2021. The team believe that it was easier to get started than initially expected. The workshop helped them get up and running quickly and to understand the value of infrastructure as code. They will share the knowledge within the team to ensure that more people understand how Terraform works and also to gain insights into what resources they are using in Azure.

They mentioned that it would be beneficial to inform the team when starting the migration that Terraform is a tool that we would like them to use and explain why as well as ensure them that there will be assistance along the way.

Akamai

The team believes that it would be beneficial to have an on-boarding of sorts regarding Akamai. It is obvious that production lives on Akamai and how to get your builds there, but other than that it is not super clear how it works, who to talk to when you have questions or where to find information.

AP DevOps team: Add entry point documentation for AKAMAI

Communication

The communication between the team and the DevOps team during the migration has worked well. The team believes that setting up a Slack channel for direct communication was extremely helpful and resulted in them moving faster. They did not feel that they needed a specific resource assigned, it was enough to have a space to ask questions and be helped.

AP DevOps team:

Decide if DevOps should have general channel in Slack as well, in addition to DevOps channel in Teams.

Archive “GitHub migration channel” after OK from Ordna team

Bottlenecks

There are some bottlenecks that have slowed the team down slightly but they have tried to plan around those. These are for example creating new repositories in Github or ordering new subscriptions on Azure. This is due to the way the IKEA IT organization is setup but we should look into if this can be improved.

Documentation

The DevOps teams documentation on Confluence has not been advertised in a good enough manner, the team weren’t aware that it existed. We need to not only improve the quality of the material, but also ensure that everyone is aware where to find it. A suggestion was to send out a reminder with some links a short while after the onboarding meeting where we sent out the welcome email.

Other suggestions

Sentry is used by Ordna and would be a good candidate to be included in DevOps setup.
